summary: NHLR Seminole County Fire Tower: 1952 Georgia Forestry Commission, 100 ft Aermotor, last staffed 1988; identity with the tnlandforms donalsonville point unconfirmed.

facts.status_note: Register says it is still operational for emergencies; the entry is dated 2008 and the link to the donalsonville record is unconfirmed.

events.note: Register gives 1952 as the completion year, by the Georgia Forestry Commission.
September 1952 state magazine: forest engineer inspected Seminole County for lookout sites; towers to be erected as steel became available. A plan, not a completion record.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 2, 2008.

evidence.supports: tnlandforms: donalsonville entry in Seminole County at 31.03052,-84.85054, elevation 171, tagged nhlr?

notes_for_editor: Identity is the main open question. The tnlandforms donalsonville row (31.03052,-84.85054, 171) and the NHLR Seminole County Fire Tower (31.024510,-84.879860, 142 ft) are about 3 km apart with different elevations; the tnlandforms row is tagged nhlr?. The story says 'most likely' and does not treat them as one site. If the editor confirms the link, the NHLR registration (US 717, GA 12, 2008-01-02) can go on the record; the brief has no registers. Built 1952 and staffed-last 1988 come from the register alone; the 1952 magazine is a plan. The 'still operational' statement is undated. Elevation units assumed feet (list gives none). No access or visit source found.
